title: Audit-tokenization-and-rbac-reconciliation-playbook-2025
author: Maya Chen
content:
> **Archived 2025-09-14:** this page is superseded by "Data-residency-aware-audit-tokenization-and-rbac-reconciliation-playbook" and is kept for reference only.

Summary:

This playbook covers how Redwood tokenizes audit events so that cross-border residency rules are respected while RBAC reconciliation and forensic fidelity are preserved. Goals: (1) keep audit evidence within legal residency boundaries, (2) retain proof of authorization decisions for investigations, and (3) keep sensitive PII and customer data out of long-term cross-region stores.

Scope:
- Systems: Redwood-Audit (event pipeline), Redwood-Authz (authorization decisions), Redwood-LogStore (hot storage), Redwood-Evidence (immutable packaging).
- Regions: us-west-2, eu-central-1, ap-southeast-1.
- Out of scope: application telemetry owned by app teams, and third-party SaaS logs not ingested into Redwood-Audit.

Definitions:
- Tokenization: deterministic replacement of sensitive values (user IDs, resource IDs) with reversible tokens protected by KMS-wrapped keys and per-region envelopes.
- RBAC reconciliation: replaying authorization checks against recorded inputs to confirm the roles, attributes and policies behind an allow/deny.
- Evidence bundle: an immutable zip of raw and tokenized events, policy snapshots and the KMS unwrap log, used for audits or legal holds.

Principles:
1) Residency-first: raw PII and residency-sensitive fields stay inside their legal boundary unless an evidence escrow request is approved.
2) Reconstructability: authorized auditors can reverse tokens through an approved unseal; every reversal is audited and time-boxed.
3) Minimal exposure: same-value token mapping supports reconciliation without exposing originals in cross-region analytics.
4) Separation of duties: key custody, evidence approval and forensic analysis sit with different roles.

Architecture:
- app -> Redwood-Audit (collector) -> per-region Tokenizer -> Redwood-LogStore (region-local) -> replication/retention policy -> Redwood-Evidence
- Keys: regional KMS (cms-redwood-audit-%REGION%); envelope keys in KMS; unwrap operations logged to the Audit-KMS-Events stream.

Playbook

1) Pre-deployment configuration (Security & Infra)
   1.1 Define a tokenization profile per workload: field_name, sensitivity_level, token_type (deterministic/reversible/one-way), residency_scope, retention_window_days.
   1.2 Provision KMS keys per region (cms-redwood-audit-us-west-2, cms-redwood-audit-eu-central-1, ...) with 365d CMK rotation and key policies limiting decrypt to the unseal service principals.
   1.3 Register the profile in the Redwood-Audit config-store with workload, team and data_classification labels.

2) Runtime processing (Audit Engineering)
   2.1 Example event received by the collector:

       {
         "ts": "2025-07-14T09:12:05Z",
         "actor_id": "u-1234567890",
         "resource_id": "res-aws-prod-42",
         "action": "model.deploy",
         "decision": "allow",
         "decision_context": {"roles": ["platform-admin"], "attrs": {"team": "infra"}}
       }

   2.2 Field rules:
       - actor_id -> deterministic reversible token with the regional envelope, e.g. TKN:r1:8f3a...
       - resource_id -> SHA256 prefix for indexing: idx_res = SHA256(res_id)[:12]
       - decision_context.roles -> plain text (not PII)
   2.3 The tokenized event is written to Redwood-LogStore in its originating region. Plain fields are indexed; token fields are stored but cannot be searched by plaintext unless unwrapped during an authorized retrieval.

3) RBAC reconciliation (Authz & Security)
   3.1 Trigger: a customer reports unauthorized access and SRE opens an RBAC-recon request.
   3.2 Steps:
       - A: Investigator files an Evidence Unseal Request (Appendix B) with justification and legal approval; Redwood-Evidence records ticket_id, scope, region, start_ts, end_ts, approver_id.
       - B: evidence-ops requests ephemeral unwrap tokens from the regional KMS under the requester principal; each unwrap lands in the KMS-Events stream.
       - C: Tokens are reversed and the original actor/resource are fed into the Redwood-Authz simulation engine to recompute the decision path.
       - D: The reconciliation report lists policy version, role binding snapshot, attribute values and match/mismatch.

4) Forensic retrieval and packaging (Security)
   4.1 Bundles contain region-local tokenized events, KMS unwrap entries, policy and role binding snapshots, and a signed SHA256 manifest. Cross-border transfer of reconstructed PII uses a time-limited escrow zip encrypted to the requester's ephemeral RSA key, approved by Legal.
   4.2 Retention:

       | Object                    | Region storage | Retention | Residency note |
       |---------------------------|----------------|-----------|----------------|
       | Tokenized audit events    | region-local   | 180d      | not copied outside region without escrow |
       | KMS unwrap logs           | central-locked | 1095d     | metadata only replicated |
       | Evidence bundles (sealed) | region-local   | 1825d     | escrowed copies need Legal + CISO |

5) Emergency unseal (Incident Response + CISO)
   5.1 Applies to active breaches involving customer data, law enforcement requests with a valid warrant, or cross-region containment needing live attributes.
   5.2 Steps:
       - Triage call with CISO, Legal, IR lead and KMS custodian.
       - Emergency authorization token from the multi-party vault (3-of-5 approvals).
       - Emergency unwrap logged with a high-priority tag and sent to the Evidence queue.
       - Full audit of unseal operations published to the compliance portal within 5 business days.

6) SLOs (Platform Reliability)
   - Tokenization latency: 99th percentile <= 50ms per event at steady state.
   - Standard evidence package: 95% within 6 hours for ranges up to 7 days.
   - Emergency unseal acknowledgment: < 30 minutes.

7) Roles
   - Security: policy owner, approves profiles and unseal requests.
   - Audit Engineering: tokenizer and regional KMS bindings.
   - Authz Team: simulation engine and reconciliation test harness.
   - Legal & Compliance: escrow, cross-border transfers, legal hold matrix.
   - Evidence Ops: sealed bundles and chain-of-custody.

8) Evidence request checklist
   - [ ] Ticket with scope and timestamps.
   - [ ] Legal approval for cross-region or PII-bearing requests.
   - [ ] CISO or deputy sign-off for emergency unseal.
   - [ ] KMS custodian notified.

Appendix A — Tokenization profile (YAML)

profile_name: model-control-audit
fields:
  - name: actor_id
    sensitivity: high
    token_type: reversible-deterministic
    residency: [us-west-2, eu-central-1]
  - name: resource_id
    sensitivity: medium
    token_type: one-way-hash
    residency: [us-west-2]
retention_days: 180
owner: infra-security

Appendix B — Evidence Unseal Request CLI

# investigator
redwood-evidence request create --ticket "INC-2025-0311" --region eu-central-1 --start 2025-07-01T00:00:00Z --end 2025-07-02T00:00:00Z --reason "suspected unauthorized role escalation"

# Legal
redwood-evidence request approve --id REQ-2025-412 --approver "legal@redwood.com" --note "warrant-12345"

# Evidence Ops
redwood-evidence assemble --id REQ-2025-412 --out /tmp/evidence-REQ-2025-412.zip

Console audit signals:
- KMS unwrap events (principal, key_id, timestamp, ticket_id)
- Bundle manifest checksums and signer
- Reconciliation outcomes by policy version
- Anomalies: repeated unwraps, partial unseals, cross-region export attempts

Governance:
- Quarterly tokenization profile review (Security).
- Annual emergency unseal tabletop with Legal, CISO and Evidence Ops.

Contacts:
- Evidence Ops: evidence-ops@redwood.com
- KMS Custodian: kms-custody@redwood.com
- Security Pager: sec-oncall@redwood.com
